headline: NASA's X-59 hits Mach 1.4 at 55,000 feet for quiet supersonic flight tests
summary: NASA's X-59 research plane recently flew at Mach 1.4 and 55,000 feet, demonstrating capabilities for its mission to create a "quiet sonic thump" instead of a traditional boom.
details: NASA's X-59 research plane recently achieved Mach 1.4 (about 924 mph) and an altitude of 55,000 feet in a test flight. This follows its first supersonic flight earlier in the month, where it hit Mach 1.1. These milestones are crucial for its upcoming mission.
The X-59 is specifically designed to fly at supersonic speeds without producing a loud sonic boom. Instead, it aims to create a "quiet sonic thump," a key innovation in supersonic flight technology.

The latest test flight was a critical step, hitting targets that will be replicated during its Quesst mission. Currently, the X-59 flies alongside another research craft to obscure its noise during testing.

The Quesst mission, still months away, will involve flying the X-59 over populated areas. NASA will then gather public feedback on the sound of the "sonic thump" from listeners on the ground. An acoustic validation phase will precede this to measure its unique supersonic signature.
